articles.title: Cancer patient told she will get drug which could make her life longer
articles.summary: Patients in England with an incurable breast cancer can now access a life-extending drug on the NHS.
articles.body:
Patients in England with a specific type of incurable breast cancer can now access a life-extending drug on the NHS.

Enhertu can give patients almost seven extra months to live on average.

Women in Scotland have had access to the drug on the NHS since 2023, and it is available in 26 other European countries.

Doctors in England are now able to prescribe it, with Wales expected to follow shortly but the guidance doesn't automatically apply to Northern Ireland.

Kate Wills, 51, has HER2-low metastatic breast cancer, which has spread to her bones and lungs.

When she hears it will be available on the NHS, she immediately starts crying. "I really can't believe it. I'm so relieved, I'm overjoyed," she says.

"It's so hard keeping hope when you have stage four cancer. This gives me enormous hope."

articles.title: Mike Tyson bought a 51,000-sq-ft Connecticut mansion for $3 million in 1996; he sold it to 50 Cent for $4.1 million and it is now back for $9.9 million
articles.summary: News News: A mansion can become famous for its architecture, its size or the people who once lived there. This 51,000-square-foot Connecticut estate has a histor.
articles.body: A mansion can become famous for its architecture, its size or the people who once lived there. This 51,000-square-foot Connecticut estate has a history that combines all three. According to The New York Post, Mike Tyson bought the Farmington property for about $3 million in 1996, before selling it to rapper 50 Cent for $4.1 million in 2003. During 50 Cent’s ownership, the mansion became a creative base where he worked on his 2005 album ‘The Massacre’. After another sale in 2019, the property underwent more than $3 million in renovations. It was back on the market for $9.9 million, with 19 bedrooms, seven kitchens and extensive entertainment spaces.Mike Tyson bought the Farmington estate before selling it to 50 CentWhen Mike Tyson purchased the Connecticut property in 1996, he paid about $3 million for a residence that was already far removed from an ordinary family home. Reportedly, the estate sits in Farmington, roughly between New York and Boston, and its size gave the former heavyweight champion plenty of room for private facilities and entertainment spaces.As reported by CBS News, Tyson remained the owner for several years before selling the mansion in 2003. The buyer was Curtis Jackson, better known as 50 Cent, who paid approximately $4.1 million.The transaction marked the beginning of another high-profile chapter for the house. For the rapper, the property was not simply a large residence. It also became a place connected to his music career.The mansion had a recording studio, cinema, pools and game roomsOne of the property's more unusual features is its recording studio. 50 Cent worked there on his 2005 album ‘The Massacre’, giving the house a connection to one of the better-known releases of his career.The mansion's entertainment facilities went well beyond the studio. There were multiple game rooms and a movie theatre, while the estate also included spaces that could accommodate large gatherings.Its sporting and recreational facilities added to the property's already considerable footprint. Indoor and outdoor pools sit alongside sports courts, while the grounds include a playground and a pond with a dock.For a house that measures roughly 51,000 square feet, there is plenty of room for spaces that would normally be spread across several separate properties.The $2.9 million purchase that led to a $3 million renovationDespite its size and celebrity history, the mansion spent years on the market before its next major change of ownership. Casey and Shera Askar bought it from 50 Cent in 2019 for $2.9 million. The couple, who are primarily based in Florida, run a portfolio of restaurants and franchises and planned to use the Connecticut property as a retreat for their family.They have seven children and used the house during summer and holiday periods. Rather than simply moving in and leaving the existing layout untouched, they saw an opportunity to reshape the property around the way their family used it.More than $3 million was subsequently spent on renovations and customisation.The renovations added a nightclub and upgraded the pool areaSome of the changes were practical, while others leaned into the unusual character of the mansion. The Askars added a cigar lounge and renovated the indoor pool and spa area. The updated space now includes a steam room, a red-light therapy sauna, a massage area and a hair salon.The kitchen was also upgraded. A commercial-grade setup was fitted with a pizza oven and dough mixer, making it possible to cater for the large groups that regularly gathered at the property. Then there is Club TKO, the house's private nightclub. Its name references Tyson's boxing career and gives one of the property's entertainment spaces a direct link to its earlier owner.The family also brought in barbers for gatherings, turning some visits into full-scale occasions rather than simple weekends away.The mansion was designed for large gatheringsThe Askars used the estate for family celebrations as well as parties and corporate events. One recent occasion was a 50th wedding anniversary celebration for Shera's parents.The sheer number of facilities made the property suitable for events involving large groups. There are 19 bedrooms, seven kitchens and several different entertainment areas, meaning visitors can be spread throughout the house rather than relying on a handful of shared rooms. There is also a green-screen room intended for photographs and videos, alongside the cinema and game rooms.The outdoor space adds another layer. The 17-acre grounds include a tennis court, playground and pond, as well as outdoor areas for entertaining.The 51,000-square-foot mansion no longer fits the family’s needsThe decision to sell is tied to a fairly ordinary change in family life, despite the unusual setting. Most of the Askars' seven children are now grown, reducing the need for a property designed to accommodate such a large household and frequent gatherings.For several years, however, the mansion served as a summer and holiday base. The owners have described family occasions there as some of their most memorable gatherings, with the property's size allowing relatives and guests to stay together under one roof.That use also explains some of the renovation choices. The pool and spa improvements, large kitchen, salon, entertainment rooms and nightclub were not simply decorative additions. Uma aposta de Bragança Paulista , no interior de São Paulo, faturou R$ 30 mil no sorteio 6.101 da Loteria Federal, realizado pela Caixa Econômica na noite desta quarta-feira (16).

O bilhete, de número 011411 foi adquirido na Pimentel Loterias, que fica na região central da cidade. Ele foi o terceiro sorteado nesta quarta e o prêmio principal, de R$ 500 mil, saiu para uma aposta de Varginha (MG).

Em operação desde 1962, a Loteria Federal é um dos prêmios mais tradicionais da Caixa. Para participar, é preciso escolher o bilhete exposto nas casas lotéricas ou com um ambulante lotérico credenciado.

A partir disso, o concorrente escolhe o número impresso no bilhete que quer concorrer, conforme disponibilização no momento da compra. Cada bilhete contém 10 frações e pode ser adquirido inteiro (R$ 40) ou em partes (R$ 4 cada).

articles.title: Menino de um ano viraliza ao dançar música gaúcha em frente à TV no RS | G1
articles.standfirst: Joaquim, de São Luiz Gonzaga, balança o corpo ao som de artistas regionais. Pais afirmam que criança rejeita outros ritmos e planejam inseri-lo em um Centro de Tradições Gaúchas.
articles.summary: Joaquim, de São Luiz Gonzaga, balança o corpo ao som de artistas regionais. Pais afirmam que criança rejeita outros ritmos e planejam inseri-lo em um Centro de Tradições Gaúchas
articles.body:
Um menino de apenas um ano e três meses está fazendo sucesso nas redes sociais ao aparecer dançando em frente à televisão , enquanto na tela são exibidos videoclipes de artistas da música gaúcha .

Vestindo traje típico, Joaquim Sztormoweski Machado, de São Luiz Gonzaga (RS), balança o corpo no ritmo das canções e já demonstra uma paixão que surpreende pela pouca idade.

O pai, o empresário Júnior Machado, conta que uma das primeiras músicas que despertou a atenção do menino foi "No Fundo da Grota", de Baitaca .

"Ele sempre quis escutar música gaúcha. A gente colocava outros tipos de música e ele sinalizava com a cabeça ou com a mãozinha que não queria. Ele aprendeu a gostar da nossa música", conta Júnior.

Com o tempo, o menino aprendeu os movimentos e passou a dançar sozinho, como aparece no vídeo.

"Ele acha a coisa mais linda. A gente fica sempre realizado com isso", afirma o pai.

Júnior e Rayane, mãe de Joaquim, já conversam sobre colocar o menino em um CTG.

"Para nós, que moramos em São Luiz Gonzaga, isso aqui é a tradição. A gente está sempre incentivando o Joaquim para ele pegar gosto pela nossa cultura", diz.

articles.summary: As imagens da invasão, que contou com uma perseguição de drone e terminou com a prisão do homem, foram registradas pelas câmeras de segurança da residência e viralizaram nas redes sociais.

As câmeras de segurança de uma residência em San Diego , nos Estados Unidos , registraram o momento em que um homem invadiu o local, no começo do mês, aproveitando que ele estava desocupado.

No entanto, o que era para ser um vídeo angustiante acabou viralizando nas redes sociais de forma divertida graças ao cachorro do dono da casa.

O vídeo, que foi postado no Instagram na segunda-feira (14), mostra o passo a passo da invasão. Ele teve mais de 6,6 milhões visualizações na rede e, nesta quarta-feira (16), virou notícia na imprensa americana.

articles.title: Cuidador é flagrado dando água sanitária para paciente nos EUA | G1
articles.standfirst: O crime foi flagrado pelas câmeras de segurança instaladas pela família e o homem foi preso.
articles.summary: O crime foi flagrado pelas câmeras de segurança instaladas pela família e o homem foi preso. Vítima tem deficiência física e mental.
articles.body:
Um cuidador foi flagrado dando água sanitária para seu paciente beber e acabou sendo preso, em Lake Charles, na Lousiana, no sul dos Estados Unidos .

O crime ocorreu na segunda-feira (14) e as imagens, feitas pelas câmeras de segurança instaladas pela família na residência, foram entregues à polícia e divulgadas nas redes sociais.

A vítima tem deficiência física e mental e é incapaz de cuidar de si mesma.

"Beba isto aqui", diz o cuidador para o paciente após colocar o produto químico dentro de um copo de água.

Cuidador colocando água sanitária em copo d'água de paciente — Foto: NBC News

Reginald Andre Wilson, de 30 anos, está atrás das grades e agora irá enfrentar múltiplas acusações, entre elas a de agressão qualificada.

Ao postar as imagens no Facebook, o irmão do paciente, Joseph Huntsberry, escreveu:

"Esse filho da p* colocou água sanitária na água do meu irmãozinho. Ele tem sorte de eu não estar em Lake Charles agora. (...) Meu irmão está numa cadeira de rodas e tem deficiência intelectual".

A empresa para qual o homem prestava serviços se pronunciou através das redes sociais e afirmou estar "profundamente triste com o ocorrido": "Agimos imediatamente, removemos o funcionário e transportamos o cliente para o pronto-socorro para avaliação".

articles.standfirst: Acidente fatal foi registrado na quarta-feira (16), no Jardim Imperador, em Araraquara (SP). Vítima foi identificada como André Luís Afonso Costa, de 43 anos.
articles.summary: Acidente fatal foi registrado na quarta-feira (16), no Jardim Imperador, em Araraquara (SP). Vítima foi identificada como André  Luís Afonso Costa, de 43 anos.
articles.body:
Motociclista André Luís Afonso Costa, de 43 anos, morreu após colidir contra árvore em Araraquara (SP) — Foto: Redes sociais

Um motociclista de 43 anos morreu após bater contra uma árvore , no Jardim Imperador, em Araraquara (SP), na quarta-feira (16). A vítima foi identificada como André Luís Afonso Costa .

O Serviço de Atendimento Móvel de Urgência (Samu) foi acionado e prestou atendimento no local, mas o motociclista não resistiu aos ferimentos e morreu na Santa Casa de Araraquara.

Segundo familiares, André teria perdido o controle da moto por motivos desconhecidos e se chocou contra uma árvore.

O corpo de André é velado nesta quinta-feira (17), no Velório São Vicente, em Franca. O sepultamento acontece às 16h, no Cemitério Jardim das Oliveiras. Ele deixa a esposa, quatro filhos, familiares e amigos.

articles.title: Rocha Empreendimentos amplia atuação com novos projetos e formas de morar | G1
articles.standfirst: Com atuação no mercado imobiliário alagoano, a construtora apresenta o Easy Rota do Mar, em Maceió, e o Vistas do Sino, em Piranhas
articles.summary: Com atuação no mercado imobiliário alagoano, a construtora apresenta o Easy Rota do Mar, em Maceió, e o Vistas do Sino, em Piranhas
articles.body:
A Rocha Empreendimentos vem construindo sua trajetória no mercado imobiliário de Alagoas com projetos que buscam unir localização estratégica, funcionalidade, qualidade construtiva e experiências que vão além do imóvel. Com o propósito de “Viver além do comum”, a construtora desenvolve empreendimentos atentos às transformações das cidades e às novas necessidades de quem busca um lugar para morar, investir ou construir novas histórias.

Entre os projetos que representam esse momento da empresa está o Easy Rota do Mar, novo empreendimento residencial da Rocha em Maceió. Localizado na Serraria, o projeto está inserido em uma região residencial estratégica, com facilidade de acesso a diferentes pontos da capital alagoana.

O Easy Rota do Mar nasce com uma proposta voltada para quem busca praticidade no dia a dia sem abrir mão de conforto e qualidade de vida. Sua localização favorece a mobilidade e aproxima os moradores de serviços, comércio e importantes vias de acesso da cidade, tornando o empreendimento uma alternativa tanto para quem deseja conquistar o próprio imóvel quanto para quem observa o potencial de valorização da região.

Vistas do Sino: um novo olhar para Piranhas

A expansão da Rocha Empreendimentos também chega ao Sertão de Alagoas com o Vistas do Sino, projeto desenvolvido em Piranhas, um dos destinos mais emblemáticos do estado.

Empreendimento Vista do Sino em Piranhas/AL — Foto: Reprodução: Construtora Rocha

Reconhecida por sua arquitetura histórica, pelas paisagens do Rio São Francisco e por sua forte vocação turística, Piranhas recebe um empreendimento que busca dialogar com as características únicas da região.

A chegada do empreendimento também representa um novo movimento da Rocha para além da capital, levando sua atuação a regiões com potencial de desenvolvimento e valorização imobiliária. Em Piranhas, a proposta é oferecer uma nova possibilidade para quem deseja desfrutar da cidade, ter um imóvel em um dos principais destinos turísticos de Alagoas ou enxergar a região como oportunidade de investimento.

Com o Easy Rota do Mar e o Vistas do Sino, a Rocha Empreendimentos reforça uma estratégia de crescimento pautada pela escolha de localizações com potencial e pelo desenvolvimento de projetos conectados ao contexto de cada região.

Mais do que construir imóveis, a Rocha busca criar espaços capazes de acompanhar diferentes momentos da vida e contribuir para o desenvolvimento dos lugares onde está presente. Uma visão que traduz o propósito da construtora e orienta seus novos projetos: Viver além do comum.

articles.title: Trump promove cerco a instituições culturais em Washington | G1
articles.standfirst: Presidente dos EUA determina encerramento do Centro Kennedy e interfere no Smithsonian para impor seu nome e sua visão sobre a História americana.
articles.summary: Presidente dos EUA determina encerramento do Centro Kennedy e interfere no Smithsonian para impor seu nome e sua visão sobre a História americana.
articles.body:
O presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, fala com repórteres antes de embarcar no Air Force One na Base Aérea Conjunta Andrews, em Maryland, em 9 de setembro de 2026. — Foto: Foto de BRENDAN SMIALOWSKI/AFP

Duas prestigiadas instituições culturais de Washington D.C. estão sob ataque do presidente dos EUA. O Centro de Artes Cênicas John F. Kennedy fechou as portas e só será reformado se o nome de Donald Trump for novamente incluído na fachada.

Por ordem do presidente, placas serão instaladas na entrada do Museu Nacional de História Americana Smithsonian com o objetivo de alertar os visitantes sobre o viés ideológico apresentado em seu interior.

A obsessão de Trump por renomear locais e monumentos para exaltar o seu legado parece não ter limites. No caso do Kennedy Center, ele esbarrou na ordem judicial , que removeu o seu nome do centro de artes. Desde o início do mandato, a instituição já havia sido tomada por conselheiros nomeados pelo presidente. Sob protestos, artistas cancelaram apresentações, e as vendas de ingressos despencaram.

O presidente decidiu então que o prédio entraria em reformas e seria fechado por dois anos. Mas o juiz federal Christopher Cooper considerou ilegal acrescentar nome de Trump ao do ex-presidente Kennedy, sem a aprovação do Congresso. E voltou a bloquear, nesta terça-feira (15), a mudança sugerida pelo Conselho, do qual Trump é presidente, renomeando a praça em frente com o seu nome.

Irritado, Trump correu para a sua rede social. Ameaçou fechar o Centro Kennedy e cancelar a remodelação se a ordem judicial não fosse revertida. “O fechamento ocorrerá imediatamente, porém, a reforma e reconstrução, que é um trabalho muito grande e complexo, não poderá começar até que o Tribunal do Circuito de DC se pronuncie sobre o nome aprovado pelo conselho”, escreveu.

E foi o que aconteceu: na terça-feira o conselho escolhido por Trump anunciou o encerramento do Centro Kennedy por tempo indeterminado. A congressista democrata Joyce Beatty, membro ex officio da entidade desde 2019, contou ter sido insultada pelo presidente , que teria tido um ataque de fúria, em uma ligação telefônica aos membros do conselho, ao saber da decisão judicial.

“Foi a coisa mais antiprofissional que já presenciei. Ele começou a me xingar, tentando me chamar de obstrucionista, dizendo que eu era burra e incompetente.” Segundo Beatty, o presidente disse que ela seria responsabilizada caso alguém morresse pelas más condições do prédio.

A insistência de Trump em renomear prédios não agrada aos americanos e representa um desgaste político para o presidente. Uma pesquisa Economist/YouGov realizada em julho mostrou que 54% aprovaram a remoção do nome de Trump do prédio, enquanto 24% disseram ser contra.

O cerco presidencial ao Smithsonian Institution, que abriga o maior complexo de museus e pesquisas do mundo, também foi declarado. As placas a serem instaladas em frente ao Museu Nacional de História Americana alertarão sobre o que o governo chama de visão tendenciosa da instituição sobre a História do país apresentada em suas exposições.

A Casa Branca enviou no ano passado uma carta ao Smithsonian instruindo seus museus a se alinharem com a visão do presidente , relatou o “Wall Street Journal”. As placas, financiadas pelo governo ao custo de US$ 84 mil (cerca de R$ 432,5 mil), refletirão a ordem executiva de Trump de julho denominada “Restaurando a confiança na Smithsonian Institution”.

O decreto presidencial acusava a instituição de “promover narrativas que retratam valores americanos e ocidentais como inerentemente nocivos e opressivos”. Em outra carta, destinada ao senador democrata Jeff Merkley, que integra a subcomissão de Orçamento responsável pelo financiamento do Smithsonian, o secretário do Interior, Doug Burgum, acusa os curadores de transformarem o museu em “um veículo para ideologias pessoais e radicais”.

A pressão do governo se intensifica com ameaças de cortar o apoio de agências federais à instituição e levou o secretário da instituição, Lonnie G. Bunch III, o primeiro negro a comandar a instituição, a anunciar, na semana passada, a aposentadoria.

“Este é mais um passo em uma campanha de pressão bem planejada pelo governo Trump para minar a integridade e a independência da Smithsonian Institution”, resumiu o senador Merkley.

articles.standfirst: Reginaldo Lima será o quarto entrevistado da série do JMTV1 com candidatos ao governo do Maranhão nas eleições de 2026; g1 Maranhão transmite ao vivo.
articles.summary: Reginaldo Lima será o quarto entrevistado da série do JMTV1 com candidatos ao governo do Maranhão nas eleições de 2026; g1 Maranhão transmite ao vivo.
articles.body:
PCB lança Reginaldo Lima como candidato ao governo do Maranhão — Foto: Divulgação

Reginaldo Lima ( PCB ) participa nesta quinta-feira (17) da série de entrevistas do JMTV 1ª Edição com os candidatos ao Governo do Maranhão nas eleições de 2026. A conversa será exibida ao vivo pela TV Mirante, durante o telejornal, que começa às 11h45, com transmissão também pelo g1 Maranhão .

O candidato do PCB é o quarto a participar da série de entrevistas, que segue até a próxima segunda-feira (21).

O JMTV 1ª Edição começa às 11h45 . A entrevista com o candidato será exibida ao vivo durante o telejornal e terá duração de 30 minutos. O público também poderá acompanhar a transmissão pelo g1 Maranhão. A conversa será conduzida pelos jornalistas Tayse Feques e Rodrigo Bomfim .

Durante a entrevista, o candidato responderá a perguntas elaboradas por 32 estudantes maranhenses , que representarão os eleitores durante a dinâmica . Os estudantes ficarão posicionados atrás do candidato e dos apresentadores.

As perguntas serão colocadas em uma urna e sorteadas ao vivo. Além dos questionamentos preparados pelos estudantes, o candidato também deverá responder a perguntas enviadas pelos eleitores.

A TV Mirante realiza, de segunda-feira (14) até o dia 21 de setembro, a série de entrevistas com os candidatos ao Governo do Maranhão nas eleições de 2026.

A ordem dos candidatos, assim como os dias e horários das entrevistas, foi definida por sorteio realizado no dia 6 de setembro , na presença de representantes das candidaturas, durante reunião no Grupo Mirante.

articles.title: Fundo Social de Santos arrecada doações para o Vale do Ribeira | G1
articles.standfirst: Entidade recebe alimentos, produtos de higiene, água, fraldas, ração e outros itens até sexta-feira (18), na sede do Fundo Social, na Encruzilhada.
articles.summary: O Fundo Social de Santos arrecada alimentos e itens de higiene para ajudar as vítimas das chuvas no Vale do Ribeira até esta sexta-feira (18).
articles.body:
Itens arrecadados pelo Fundo Social de Santos serão destinados a moradores afetados pelas fortes chuvas no Vale Do Ribeira (SP). — Foto: Divulgação/Prefeitura de Santos

O Fundo Social de Solidariedade (FSS) de Santos está arrecadando doações para moradores afetados pelas fortes chuvas no Vale do Ribeira. As doações podem ser entregues das 9h às 18h, na Avenida Conselheiro Nébias, 388, no bairro Encruzilhada.

A campanha recebe alimentos não perecíveis, materiais de limpeza, produtos de higiene pessoal, água, fraldas descartáveis, leite e ração para animais até sexta-feira (18).

Nesta terça-feira (15), o FSS enviou 500 quilos de alimentos, mais de 1,5 mil peças de roupas femininas, masculinas e infantis e cobertores ao Fundo Social de Registro . Os itens serão utilizados nos postos de acolhimento que atendem moradores afetados.

As doações enviadas já faziam parte do estoque da instituição, formado por meio da campanha permanente de arrecadação mantida pelo município.

O Rio Ribeira de Iguape transbordou e provocou alagamentos em Registro e Sete Barras nesta quarta-feira (16). Em Registro, 28 famílias precisaram deixar suas casas e o município teve a situação de emergência homologada pelo Governo de São Paulo.

Em Sete Barras , outras 25 famílias estão desabrigadas. Pariquera-Açu também registra pontos de alagamento em áreas rurais. Já em Ribeira, Iporanga e Eldorado , onde 80% da área urbana ficou debaixo d'água, a situação começou a melhorar e moradores realizam a limpeza das casas.

articles.title: Receber na chácara: a estrutura mínima que evita improviso | G1
articles.standfirst: Convidar trinta pessoas para o sítio expõe o que falta na área de lazer. Veja a estrutura mínima que resolve o dia sem correria de última hora
articles.summary: Convidar trinta pessoas para o sítio expõe o que falta na área de lazer. Veja a estrutura mínima que resolve o dia sem correria de última hora
articles.body:
Toda propriedade nova passa pelo mesmo teste: o primeiro almoço com muita gente. É nesse dia que se descobre que falta lugar para a brasa, que a mesa não comporta todos e que o gelo acabou às duas da tarde. Montar a estrutura mínima antes evita transformar o convite em corre-corre.

Churrasqueiras a bafo: capacidade para grupo grande com menos supervisão — Foto: Divulgação / Panela de Ferro Fundido

Por que o bafo facilita receber muita gente

Churrasqueira aberta exige alguém em pé, virando carne, o tempo todo — normalmente o anfitrião, que fica fora da festa. Com a tampa fechada, o calor circula por todos os lados e a carne assa por igual sem virada constante. Isso libera quem cozinha e permite assar peças grandes de uma vez, em vez de fatia por fatia.

Churrasqueira aberta prende o anfitrião de pé virando carne. A tampa fechada devolve o dia a ele.

•Ponto de brasa dimensionado para o número de convidados, não para a família.

•Área coberta: chuva de verão em Minas não pede licença.

•Mesa e assento para o grupo — banco de jardim resolve volume com pouco espaço.

•Iluminação externa: o almoço sempre vira noite.

•Panela grande para acompanhamento: feijão tropeiro e arroz não caem na churrasqueira.

•Local para lixo definido, ou o quintal amanhece coberto.

O erro clássico é comprar churrasqueira do tamanho da família e usar em festa. Se você costuma receber grupo, dimensione para isso — assar em três rodadas significa que o primeiro grupo termina antes do último começar. Modelos de tambor e com carrinho existem justamente para volume alto.

Modelos de tambor e com rodas: volume para grupo grande em uma só rodada — Foto: Divulgação / Panela de Ferro Fundido

Dimensionar pelo maior evento, e não pela média, é o que evita a segunda rodada. As churrasqueiras a bafo vão do modelo compacto ao tambor com carrinho.

Sediada em Divinópolis , no Centro-Oeste de Minas, a Panela de Ferro Fundido trabalha com churrasqueiras e peças para área de lazer. Os modelos estão no catálogo de churrasqueiras a bafo , com entrega para todo o Brasil.

articles.title: Acidentes na Rodovia do Açúcar bloqueiam faixa da pista em Piracicaba | G1
articles.standfirst: Colisões foram registradas na rodovia na manhã desta quinta-feira (17). Um pessoa teve ferimentos leves, segundo concessionária responsável pelo trecho.
articles.summary: Acidentes na Rodovia do Açúcar em Piracicaba envolveram carros, caminhonete e moto nesta quinta-feira, causando bloqueios e lentidão no trânsito.
articles.body:
A Rodovia do Açúcar (SP-08) registrou seis acidentes em sequência na manhã desta quinta-feira (17) em Piracicaba (SP). Uma das faixas da pista, perto da região do pontilhão da Avenida Dois Córregos, ficou interditada. Houve congestionamento de três quilômetros e lentidão no trânsito, segundo a concessionária responsável pelo trecho.

A concessionária Rodovias do Tietê informou ao g1 , na manhã desta quinta-feira, que o primeiro acidente envolveu uma motocicleta e um veículo utilitário por volta das 7h e interditou a faixa 2 da Rodovia do Açúcar (SP-308), no Km 126, no sentido Piracicaba (SP).

Rodovia do Açúcar registra acidentes e faixa da pista tem trânsito lento em Piracicaba — Foto: Edijan Del Santo/EPTV

O motociclista sofreu ferimentos leves, foi atendido no local e encaminhado à Santa Casa de Piracicaba, enquanto o ocupante do outro veículo saiu ileso do acidente.

A interdição da faixa gerou lentidão na região, o que acabou provocando outras cinco colisões traseiras leves e sem vítimas nos quilômetros 162, 160, 159 e duas ocorrências no quilômetro 157 da Rodovia do Açúcar.

Rodovia do Açúcar em Piracicaba registra acidentes — Foto: Edijan Del Santo/EPTV

As outras colisões, envolvram carros de passeio em trecho mais distante do pontilhão, segundo apuração da EPTV . Um dos acidentes ocorreu entre um carro e uma caminhonete. As vítimas foram retiradas do local.

O reflexo de todas essas ocorrências resultou em três quilômetros de lentidão no trânsito.

Acidentes bloqueiam faixa da Rodovia do Açúcar em Piracicaba — Foto: Edijan Del Santo/EPTV

O trânsito tinha começado a ser liberado por volta das 8h15. Mas, até às 8h45, ainda havia lentidão no trecho.

Equipes da Polícia Rodoviária trabalharam no atendimento às ocorrências.

Por volta das 9h30, o tráfego fluía normalmente no local. Alguns veículos envolvidos aguardam remoção pelos canteiros lateral e central, sendo uma motocicleta, um utilitário e dois veículos de passeio.

Os demais envolvidos já deixaram a via por meios próprios.

articles.title: Vestibular de Medicina Facape: inscrições abertas para 53 cidades | G1
articles.standfirst: Provas presenciais acontecem em 25 de outubro. Recentemente, curso ganhou nova policlínica no Centro de Petrolina com 18 consultórios para aulas práticas.
articles.summary: O vestibular de Medicina da Facape oferece bolsas integrais e aulas práticas na nova policlínica de Petrolina; as provas presenciais ocorrem em 25 de outubro.
articles.body:
A Faculdade de Petrolina está com inscrições abertas para o Vestibular Regional de Medicina. — Foto: Divulgação/ Facape

A Faculdade de Petrolina ( Facape ), em Pernambuco, abriu inscrições para o vestibular Regional de Medicina. O processo seletivo oferece vagas exclusivas para moradores de 53 cidades pernambucanas e baianas.

Os interessados podem se inscrever até o dia 13 de outubro pelo site da instituição . Já a prova presencial vai acontecer no dia 25 de outubro.

O vestibular também contempla ações de inclusão social. Ao todo, serão ofertadas três bolsas integrais no curso de Medicina: sendo uma destinada para estudantes egressos de escolas públicas que tenham cursado integral, exclusiva e regularmente os anos finais do Ensino Fundamental (6º ao 9º ano) e todos os anos do ensino médio. E duas vagas para estudantes de baixa renda.

Políclinica da Facape — Foto: Divulgação/ Facape

Recentemente, o curso inaugurou a nova sede da Policlínica Facape, localizada na Praça do Coliseu, no Centro da cidade. O espaço tem 18 consultórios, além de salas de procedimentos e de orientação, com foco na formação prática dos alunos.

Atualmente, cerca de 200 universitários são acompanhados por 19 médicos em 13 áreas de atuação. Entre as especialidades oferecidas estão pediatria, geriatria, ginecologia, clínica geral, cardiologia, neurologia e ortopedia.

articles.title: Temporary tidal barriers to be tested in flood-prone Lowestoft
articles.summary: The dry run will give teams the chance to practise how they would respond to a real flood.
articles.body:
Temporary tidal barriers designed to protect against a coastal surge are to be put to the test in a flood-prone town ahead of the winter.

The trial will be carried out between Commercial Road East and Lake Lothing in Lowestoft, Suffolk, on Thursday, from 19:00 BST until 22:00.

The dry run will give local authority teams the opportunity to practise how they would need to respond in the event of a real flood.

Councillor Mark Packard, East Suffolk's cabinet member for planning and coastal management, said being able to simulate the emergency was "important".

He added doing so ensured both the authority's defences and deployment teams would be ready to respond in the event of a North Sea tidal surge.

"The exercise is an important opportunity for our teams to trial putting up the defences to ensure they can be safely and efficiently deployed," he said.

Concerns about the possibility of Lowestoft being submerged by floods have long been a contentious topic of discussion among residents and council officials.

In 2013, the town was devastated by flooding when a powerful tidal surge damaged buildings and disrupted essential services and businesses.

One of those businesses was Alpine Fabrication, on Commercial Road, which was left 1m (3ft) under water, while Doe Metal Recycling suffered £60,000 worth of damage.

The effects of the flood were so severe that a £199m Lowestoft Flood Protection scheme was considered, with a view to putting in place a permanent barrier.

It was designed to protect more than 1,500 homes and 800 businesses - but was axed in January 2024 due to rising costs and a funding shortfall of more than £124m.

The first phase of the work was completed in 2023 but the council could not find the £20m for the next stage, and the government could not cover the costs.

In late 2025, campaigners renewed calls for a permanent tidal barrier to be installed, with Penny Dack saying the town would "die" without one.

The council said it was working with the Environment Agency and partners to "explore the next steps in making Lowestoft better protected from flooding".

The council said it had now allocated £100,000 from its Regional Flood and Coast Committee to engage a consultant to explore options to mitigate flood risk for Lowestoft.

"Working in collaboration with the Environment Agency and Suffolk County Council, a contract will be going out to tender for this work in the next few weeks," a spokesperson said.

"It is expected that it will take some time to receive and review the options. In the meantime, the temporary barriers will be deployed in the event of a tidal surge and used in conjunction with the completed flood walls."

articles.title: US Air Force weighs C-17 production restart; will India seek more Globemaster?
articles.summary: News News: The US Air Force is examining whether Boeing's C-17 Globemaster III production line can be revived, reopening the possibility of producing the heavy-l.
articles.body: The US Air Force is examining whether Boeing's C-17 Globemaster III production line can be revived, reopening the possibility of producing the heavy-lift aircraft more than a decade after its production ended.According to The War Zone, Air Mobility Command chief Lt Gen Daniel Tulley said the feasibility of bringing back the aircraft is being considered as part of a broader Analysis of Alternatives for the Air Force's future airlift fleet.The review will examine whether existing C-17 production tooling, machinery and the wider industrial base can be restored, how much it would cost and whether a modernised version of the aircraft could meet future requirements.The C-17 remains one of the US military's most important airlift platforms, capable of carrying heavy equipment, troops and vehicles while also operating from relatively austere airfields.TWZ also reported that Boeing has previously been approached by unnamed existing C-17 operators about the possibility of restarting production. Boeing has said it was encouraged by those discussions, although the identities of those operators have not been disclosed.The C-17 Globemaster III is a four-engine heavy military transport aircraft designed for both strategic and tactical airlift missions. Built by Boeing, it can move troops, vehicles and heavy equipment over long distances and can also land on relatively short and austere runways, giving it a role beyond conventional long-range cargo transport.It has a maximum take-off weight of roughly 265 tonnes and can carry a maximum payload of about 77.5 tonnes. The C-17 is powered by four Pratt & Whitney F117-PW-100 turbofan engines and can reach speeds of around 940 km/h.Why is the US looking to restart C-17 production?The main reason behind the renewed C-17 discussion is the US Air Force's long-term airlift requirement. C-17 remains a critical part of America's ability to move troops, vehicles, weapons and other heavy equipment rapidly across the world.The US is developing a Next Generation Airlift capability that is expected to eventually replace both the C-17A Globemaster III and the larger C-5M Galaxy. But developing, testing and deploying a completely new heavy transport aircraft could take decades. This has created a potential gap between the retirement of existing aircraft and the arrival of their successors.Instead of relying entirely on an ageing fleet until a new airlifter arrives, the US could potentially acquire additional aircraft and keep its heavy airlift capacity at the required level.The pressure on the current fleet is another factor behind the renewed C-17 debate. The US Air Force currently has 222 C-17A Globemaster III aircraft. The fleet has also seen extensive use in recent US military operations and overseas deployments, including missions in Afghanistan, Iraq, Syria, Gaza and the Middle East.The C-17 was also heavily used during the US campaign against Iran in 2026, carrying personnel, weapons and other supplies across the region.Will India be interested in acquiring more C-17s?A possible revival of C-17 production could also reopen an option for India, which operates 11 C-17 Globemaster III aircraft.In 2015, the IAF had pushed for three more C-17s to strengthen its strategic airlift fleet. However, Boeing's production line was already being shut down, and only one additional aircraft could ultimately be secured, taking India's fleet to 11.That means a production restart could give India another opportunity to expand its heavy-lift fleet. The C-17 has already demonstrated its usefulness for India in missions involving Leh, Thoise, Mechuka, Port Blair and overseas operations, where its heavy payload and short-field capability are particularly valuable.However, there is no confirmed Indian plan to buy more C-17s at present. TWZ has reported that Boeing has been approached by some existing C-17 operators regarding a possible production restart, but those countries have not been identified.

articles.title: '9/11 architects were not hiding in caves': India hits out at Pakistan at UN over terror safe havens
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: India on Wednesday hit out at Pakistan at the UN Security Council, saying Islamabad had provided a \"permissive environment\" to the \"archite.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India on Wednesday hit out at Pakistan at the UN Security Council, saying Islamabad had provided a "permissive environment" to the "architects" of the 9/11 attacks and continues to provide space and support to terror groups such as Lashkar-e-Taiba and Jaish-e-Mohammed.Speaking at a UN Security Council meeting, India's Permanent Representative P Harish recalled the 9/11 terror attacks in United States and said al-Qaida leaders Osama bin Laden and Khalid Sheikh Mohammed were eventually found in settled communities in Pakistan rather than "caves or badlands".“The international community supported the global campaign to counter terrorism in the wake of 9/11. Let us not forget, however, that al-Qaida's terror ecosystem established its strategic depth beyond Afghanistan through its affiliates,” Harish said.“The leaders of al-Qaida who conceived and directed these 9/11 attacks did not escape justice in the wilderness of some ungoverned frontier.”The Indian envoy also listed out the names of terrorists found in Pakistan.Bin Laden, who ordered and financed the 9/11 plot, was “tracked down and killed in a fortified compound within a settled, guarded community under Operation Neptune Spear”, he said.Mohammed, “the principal architect of the operation, was found sheltering in an ordinary residential house. Ramzi Binalshibh, who coordinated the hijacker cell after being denied a visa to join them, was sheltering in an urban centre,” Harish said.Senior al-Qaida operative Walid bin Attash, who helped select and prepare several hijackers, was captured separately, while Mustafa Ahmed al-Hawsawi, a key financial and logistical facilitator of the 9/11 operation, was also captured in Pakistan, he said."In each case, these were not fugitives hiding in caves or badlands, they were men who had long evaded detection. Draining this swamp that provided an enabling environment for such monsters of humankind to prosper is important," Harish said, in a thinly veiled reference to Pakistan.Harish also drew attention to what he described as an axis involving Pakistan, al-Qaida and terrorists targeting India."The same permissive environment that sheltered the architects of 9/11 has, in the years since, continued to provide space, support, and impunity to affiliates of al Qaida such as Lashkar-e-Taiba and Jaish-e-Mohammed and their like," he said.He said these groups continue to operate under different identities to evade the Council's sanctions, while their terror-training infrastructure continues to operate with impunity.The international community must act against the continued existence of such sanctuaries, he said, "to ensure that more such individuals are not thrust upon any country or its citizens and no one loses family and loved ones".Last week, as the world marked 25 years of the September 11 terror attacks perpetrated by al-Qaida, UN Security Council members, including Pakistan, visited the 9/11 memorial in Lower Manhattan.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: 1st hate-crime victim after 9/11: 25 years on, Balbir Singh Sodhi remembered
articles.summary: BATHINDA: Faith and civil rights leaders from Sikh, Muslim, Hindu, Jewish and Christian communities, along with Palestinian-American activists, came t.
articles.body: BATHINDA: Faith and civil rights leaders from Sikh, Muslim, Hindu, Jewish and Christian communities, along with Palestinian-American activists, came together in Mesa, Arizona, on Tuesday evening to remember the first victim of a hate crime in the US after the 9/11 terrorist attacks.Four days after the terror strikes that killed 2,996 people in New York, Virginia and Pennsylvania, Sikh-American gas station owner Balbir Singh Sodhi was shot dead in Mesa on September 15, 2001. Twenty-five years on, his family and community leaders gathered at the same gas station where the 52-year-old Indian immigrant was killed, remembering his life and the hate crimes that followed the attacks.His brother Rana Singh Sodhi recalled a phone conversation he had nearly a decade ago with Frank Silva Roque, who was convicted of killing Balbir. Roque had apologised, sought forgiveness and expressed a wish to meet Rana after his release. "I told him that we have already forgiven him. When he died in prison at the age of 62 in 2022, we hope he might have met Balbir, wherever he might be," Rana said.Balbir's widow and family attended the remembrance, along with grandchildren born after his death. They recalled stories about him, particularly those shared by their grandmother.Civil rights activist, filmmaker and author Valarie Kaur, whose Revolutionary Love Project organised the memorial with the Sodhi family, said it also sought to remember others who became victims of hate crimes after 9/11. "Revolutionary love is the choice to see no stranger, to leave no one outside our circle of care even to risk for each other," Kaur said.Speakers included Aasees Kaur of Sikh Coalition, Deepa Iyer of Building Movement Project, Kiran Kaur Gill of Sikh American Legal Defense and Education Fund, Zahra Billoo of Council on American-Islamic Relations, Rami Nashashibi of Inner-City Muslim Action Network, Sapna Gupta of Hindus for Human Rights, Rev Hierald E Osorto, Rabbi Sharon Brous of IKAR and Rev Michael-Ray Mathews of Prophetic Foundry.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Chandigarh | Silver Rate in Chandigarh | Bank Holidays in Chandigarh | Public Holidays in Chandigarh | Chandigarh AQI | Weather in Chandigarh | Petrol Price in Chandigarh | Diesel Price in Chandigarh | CNG Price in Chandigarh | LPG Price in ChandigarhStay updated with the latest Chandigarh news. articles.title: In 1799, a 12-year-old found a 17-pound gold rock in a North Carolina creek; used as a doorstop for 3 years, it sold for $3.50 and sparked America’s first gold rush
articles.summary: US News: In 1799, 12-year-old Conrad Reed found a 17-pound gold nugget that unknowingly sparked the U.S. gold rush. Explore the journey of this golden discovery and its impact on North Carolina's mining industry.
articles.body: In 1799, when a boy of 12 years old, named Conrad Reed was playing in Little Meadow Creek, located within Cabarrus County, North Carolina, he unearthed a heavy golden stone weighing 17 pounds and brought it home to show his father, John Reed, who was a farmer. Neither John nor his son knew the value of the stone, and the two spent the following three years living with it without realizing its importance and how important it would prove to be for their lives. The heavy stone served as a doorstop in their family house. Once the stone was identified as gold, it became part of a discovery that made North Carolina the country's leading gold producer for nearly 50 years, until the start of the California gold rush.John Reed, born Johannes Reith, settled in Cabarrus CountyThe story of John Reed, who was actually born as Johannes Reith, was rather a peculiar one. He was a Hessian soldier in the British Army during the American Revolutionary War and at its end, he deserted and settled down amongst the German-speaking community in the Piedmont area of North Carolina, according to the North Carolina Division of State Historic Sites. He anglicized his name and took up farming, raising corn and wheat.Conrad Reed finds a 17-pound rock in Little Meadow Creek, 1799This stone might definitely have remained unnoticed if Conrad had not discovered it in Little Meadow Creek in 1799 because of the unusual nature of the rock itself. Neither Conrad nor his father had known the rock's worth until three years later, when a jeweler realized it was gold. It was in 1802 that the mystery was solved when John Reed brought the rock to the jeweler in Fayetteville during his usual trip selling agricultural products. The jeweler recognized the rock as gold, worth roughly a thousand times what he then offered for it, and asked Reed to name his price. Unaware of the rock's true value, Reed asked for what he thought was a generous sum: $3.50, about a week's wages for a farmer at the time.Reed forms a four-man mining partnership, 1803Reed believed that there were more deposits of gold in the vicinity after becoming aware of the sale. In the year following this incident, Reed brought in three partners to form a mining company, making four men in total; in exchange for half the land and profits, they provided him with tools and laborers. The following year, a boy named Peter, who was enslaved, found a 28-pound gold nugget. According to the North Carolina Division of State Historic Sites, this is the biggest nugget found at the Reed Gold Mine. The discovery soon attracted the attention of Reed's neighbors.According to records in The Western Carolinian newspaper dated 1825, gold mining ranked as the second largest industry after agriculture in North Carolina. By the year 1840, North Carolina mines were producing gold worth over $1 million annually, thus making North Carolina the leading gold producer in America. North Carolina remained America's leading gold producer until 1848, when the California Gold Rush began and quickly overtook it in total production.Underground quartz mining begins at Reed's property, 1831There were changes in the mining operation that took place at Reed's estate over the following decades. At first, gold was extracted using the placer mining method from stream gravel. But soon enough, miners found out that gold could be found in veins of white quartz underground in the 1820s. Vein or lode mining was a much more costly operation than creek panning. Mining at Reed's mine began underground in 1831. Disputes in the family led to the mine's closure for ten years beginning in 1835, a closure that lasted until Reed died in 1845. His estate was sold in stages over the following decades. In 1895, it was purchased by Dr. Justin D. Lisle and the Kelly family for $15,000.Reed Gold Mine became a National Historic LandmarkThe site of Reed’s discovery remains intact today as a North Carolina state historic site and a National Historic Landmark. The tunnels have been restored, and visitors can see exhibits tracing the mine's history, from the rock a boy carried home in 1799 to the discovery that followed.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Algae bloom that crippled Israel's desalination plants raises water security concerns
articles.summary: The "carpet" of microalgae stopped five of Israel's six desalination plants from working.
articles.body:
A recent outage of nearly all of Israel's major desalination plants has sparked concern over the country's future water security, with experts warning the war in Gaza is making the situation worse.

A vast bloom of microalgae in the Mediterranean Sea that grew to 100km (62 miles) long and 7km wide at its peak clogged the filters of five of the six major plants that convert seawater into drinking water.

While they are now up and running again (although only at up to 50% capacity) the microalgae remains present after almost three weeks and there is real concern that something similar could happen again.

The microalgae is thought to have originated from the Nile Delta, with experts pointing to a northerly current around the coastal eastern Mediterranean that then swept it up to Gaza and Israel. Feeding off sunlight as well as nutrients in the water, it has since spread rapidly, driven by higher-than-normal temperatures in the Mediterranean Sea.

Some academics have suggested Israel's destruction of Gaza's sewage treatment plants in the war with Hamas is partly to blame.

"It's early days, but we know that sewage is a nutrient and algae blooms at great rates when there's lots of nutrients in its vicinity," says Gidon Bromberg of the EcoPeace Middle East environmental group.

What was the damage to Gaza's wastewater treatment plants?

Bromberg says even before the war, Israel's restrictions on what is allowed into Gaza meant the territory's sewage plants were out of date.

"One of the reasons why modern sewer stream plants weren't completed in Gaza was because in order to build and run [them] you needed equipment that the Israeli military has defined as dual use - that could be used by Hamas as a weapon," he says, giving the example of cement.

Edo Bar-Zeev, a professor at the Zuckerberg Institute for Water Research at Ben-Gurion University, called what has happened an "unexpected mega event".

"I've been in the field of sampling ocean water for around 20 years or so and it's definitely unusual," he said. "In most cases it comes and goes in a few days, maybe a week... and here it's held on for a while."

The six plants, which generate more than 60% of Israel's drinking water, were hit by what Lior Gutman, spokesman for Mekorot, Israel's national water company, called a "huge carpet of microorganisms".

Some farmers were affected, although the majority of those who use recycled water for irrigation did not face any shortages. Neither did 99% of households, Gutman said.

The fact that the water crisis was hardly noticed by Israelis is a stark contrast to the daily lives of Gazans, who struggle with clean water supplies after Israeli bombardment has destroyed 90% of the Strip's water and sanitation infrastructure, according to a report by aid organisation Doctors Without Borders.

Israel has become a world leader in desalination plants, which convert seawater into drinking water. A combination of climate change and a growing population has led Israel to rely more and more on the plants, which are located mainly along Israel's coastline.

What happened has made experts worried about how Israel's desalination plants can be paralysed by something like microalgae. Israel is also a major exporter of desalination technology, with Israeli companies designing and building plants around the world.

"I think this is a wake-up call for everyone in the water sector and certainly everyone here in the Middle East where desalination has been a major development to help advance a level of water security," said Gidon Bromberg.

articles.title: Why are pink plaques appearing across Bristol?
articles.summary: The team responsible said they celebrate key locations in culture, creativity and technology.
articles.body:
Several pink plaques have appeared overnight, celebrating locations that have seen major impacts in technology, creativity and culture.

Aardman's Creature Comforts, Nirvana's first Headline UK gig and the start of trip hop are among the influential moments marked in Bristol in the early hours of Wednesday.

Brazen, the organisation that put them up, said they were inspired by Historic England's blue plaques, showing where a historic person made a significant contribution to society.

Ben Shorrock, chief executive of TechSPARK, the group behind Brazen, said: "Bristol's influence reaches far beyond the city, from globally recognised creative work to technologies that have changed people's lives."

Business 'shocked' at double dragon investment

Low-cost food pantry awarded £272k lottery grant

Family 'devastated' as missing girl case stays closed

Those responsible said they deliberately did not ask permission, but said they can be easily removed.

One is outside The Golden Lion, where Bristol band IDLES held their first gig. Another is at Aardman's Banana Warehouse to celebrate Creature Comforts, and another in Stoke Gifford highlights the creation of the online movie database IMDb.

Other venues marked by the plaques are no longer there, including the former Bristol Bierkeller where Nirvana opened their Nevermind Tour in 1991 and the legendary nightclub the Dug Out, which was important in the development of trip hop.

The Brazen team is also organising a new five-day festival of technology, creativity and culture in Bristol from 9 to 13 November; it will feature talks, debates, technology showcases and performances.

Ben Webb, head of growth at Brazen, said: "The idea was to take inspiration from the blue plaques that you find on heritage sites, but to use pink plaques to signify key locations around Bristol that have had a global impact on technology, creativity and culture.

"They've been done somewhat under the cover of darkness in the same ilk as the innovators they celebrate, to not ask permission, just to go and do," he said.

"They've been put up to last as long as they can, but they can be removed without doing any damage to the building behind them.

"We'd be delighted if people were to keep them where they were and keep celebrating this amazing place."

articles.title: Bombs that wouldn’t explode, a bike that wouldn’t stay put: Rajasthan’s unique temples that defy every rule
articles.summary: A temple that shelters 25,000 sacred rats; one where a motorcycle is worshipped; a border shrine associated with legends of bombs that failed to explo.
articles.body: A temple that shelters 25,000 sacred rats; one where a motorcycle is worshipped; a border shrine associated with legends of bombs that failed to explode; and a healing centre where exorcism rituals unfold in plain sightRajasthan is often imagined through its forts, palaces and royal history. But beyond its grand architecture lies another Rajasthan — one where faith has taken forms that can surprise even those familiar with the state’s rich religious traditions.These temples are unusual not because their faith is lesser or different, but because each has developed a distinctive relationship between belief, legend, ritual and everyday life.Karni Mata Temple, Deshnok: The rat templeAt Deshnok near Bikaner, the Karni Mata Temple presents perhaps the most striking expression of Rajasthan’s religious traditions. The temple is dedicated to Karni Mata, a revered 14th-15th century mystic whom devotees regard as an incarnation of Goddess Durga.What sets the shrine apart is not simply its deity but the thousands of rats that freely move through its marble corridors. Known as kabbas, the rats are revered by devotees rather than treated as pests.The tradition is rooted in a deeply held legend. According to the story, Karni Mata's stepson Laxman drowned while trying to drink water from the Kapil Sarovar. She pleaded with Yama, the god of death, to restore him to life. The legend says that Yama eventually agreed, but decreed that Karni Mata's male descendants and devotees would be reincarnated as rats. The kabbas are therefore regarded as sacred reincarnations connected to Karni Mata's family and followers.Devotees feed the rats milk, grains and sweets, and food touched by them is regarded as sacred. Among the thousands of black rats, the sighting of a white rat is considered particularly auspicious and is associated with divine blessings and prosperity.Hurting or killing one of the rats is considered a serious offence within the temple's tradition.The unusual presence of the rats, however, does not overshadow the temple's architecture. The present structure was completed in the early 20th century under Maharaja Ganga Singh of Bikaner. Built largely in marble, it features ornate carvings and silver doors whose panels depict legends associated with the goddess.The inner sanctum houses a roughly 75-centimetre idol of Karni Mata holding a trident and wearing a crown and garlands. Further marble and silver embellishments were added in 1999.For devotees, the rats are not the spectacle they may appear to an outsider. They are part of the temple's sacred world — living embodiments of a centuries-old belief.Om Banna Dham, Pali: The Bullet Baba TempleOn a road in Rajasthan's Pali region stands another shrine unlike conventional temples. Here, the object at the centre of devotion is not a traditional deity but a Royal Enfield Bullet motorcycle associated with Om Singh Rathore, popularly known as Om Banna or Bullet Baba.The shrine grew from the story of Om Singh Rathore, who died in a motorcycle accident in 1988 after his bike struck a tree.According to local belief, police took the motorcycle away after the accident, but it subsequently disappeared and was found back at the accident site. The story says that attempts to remove it again met with the same result, with the motorcycle repeatedly returning to the place where Om Banna had died.The accounts are part of local legend rather than an established explanation of what happened. But the story became powerful enough to create a shrine of its own.The motorcycle, a 350cc Royal Enfield, came to be treated as a sacred object. It was placed at the accident site and gradually became known as Bullet Baba.Devotees passing through the area stop to pay their respects; others offer a brief prayer from the road. The bike is kept inside a glass enclosure and decorated with flower garlands and red cloth, while devotees have been reported applying a tilak to its headlight.The belief surrounding Om Banna is closely tied to the idea of protection. Local devotees regard his spirit as a guardian of travellers on the stretch of road associated with his death.Tanot Mata Temple, Jaisalmer: A border shrine shaped by stories of warDeep in the desert landscape of Jaisalmer, close to the India-Pakistan border, stands Tanot Mata Temple, a shrine whose religious identity became inseparable from the history of India's wars.The temple is regarded as a shrine of Tanot Mata, who is considered an incarnation of Goddess Hinglaj Mata and, in some traditions, associated with the divine mother forms of the region. The temple is described around 1,200 years old, with its origins placed in the early eighth century.Its extraordinary reputation comes from the 1965 and 1971 wars. According to accounts associated with the shrine, Pakistani shelling and bombing fell around the temple during the 1965 conflict, but many of the bombs reportedly failed to explode.For devotees, these unexploded bombs became enduring symbols of Tanot Mata's protective power. They were later preserved and displayed at the temple, turning remnants of wartime violence into objects associated with faith and remembrance.The legend grew further after the 1971 war, when the shrine became increasingly identified with divine protection. Five silver umbrellas associated with Pakistani Colonel Shahnawaz Khan are said to remain at the temple as offerings, adding another striking element to its wartime history.The temple is now managed by the Border Security Force, with BSF personnel involved in its daily rituals and worship. A temple and museum were developed after the wars, while a Vijay Stambh within the complex commemorates India's victory at Longewala.The temple's story entered contemporary military memory again during Operation Sindoor.In a 2025 news agency ANI report, BSF Commandant Neeraj Sharma attributed the destruction of Pakistani drones and missiles over Jaisalmer to Tanot Mata's blessings.Mehandipur Balaji, Dausa : A shrine associated with spiritual healingIn the hills around Rajasthan's Dausa-Karauli region, Mehandipur Balaji has acquired a reputation unlike that of an ordinary Hanuman temple.The shrine is dedicated to Lord Hanuman in his child form — hence the name Balaji. What distinguishes it is its long-standing association with ritualistic healing and exorcism, with devotees coming to the temple seeking relief from what they believe are evil spirits or negative energies.According to local lore, the idol of Balaji manifested miraculously in the surrounding hills centuries ago. The shrine subsequently became associated with the belief that the deity can protect devotees, drive away negative forces and bring relief to troubled souls.The atmosphere of the temple is shaped by chants, bells, prayers and intense rituals. Accounts describe devotees undertaking special practices for spiritual cleansing, while rituals associated with healing are performed around Balaji and the other deities within the temple complex.The sanctum is associated not only with Balaji but also with Pret Raj Sarkar and Kotwal Bhairav, figures traditionally connected with the temple's distinctive ritual system and ideas of protection and spiritual justice.Among the practices associated with the shrine are rituals known as Arji, Sawamani and Darkhast. The temple tradition also places particular emphasis on what devotees do with offerings: accounts say that certain prasad associated with these rituals is not to be consumed or taken home, but discarded according to prescribed practice.The temple's reputation has also led to reports of people displaying extreme physical and emotional behaviour during rituals, including crying, shouting or behaving as though affected by supernatural forces. Such experiences are matters of religious belief and interpretation rather than established evidence of possession.For the faithful, however, Mehandipur Balaji is a place where prayer is sought as a form of spiritual protection and relief. Its significance lies precisely in that distinctive relationship between devotion and ritual healing.Shri Sanwariya Seth Temple, Chittorgarh: God as Business PartnerIn the Mewar region's Chittorgarh district, the Shri Sanwariya Seth Temple has developed a distinctive identity around Lord Krishna as Sanwariya Seth — a form of the deity whom devotees associate not only with worship but also with prosperity and business.The temple is located in the Mandfiya-Bhadasoda region and is popularly known as Krishna Dham. Its black stone idol represents the dark complexion traditionally associated with Lord Krishna. The temple complex features carved pillars, ornate walls and pink sandstone architecture.What makes the shrine particularly distinctive is the relationship devotees believe they have with Sanwariya Seth. Many devotees consider the deity a partner in their businesses and personal earnings, offering a portion of their income as an expression of gratitude and faith. The belief has given the temple a special following among business communities.The tradition is not limited to conventional offerings. Devotees have reportedly offered silver representations of houses, petrol pumps, mobile phones and even crops.The offering is unusual, but the larger tradition reveals something deeper about the shrine: devotees often translate their worldly lives into their worship. A business, salary, property or personal achievement can become an offering to the deity they believe has shared in their prosperity.The temple's legend also connects it with Mirabai. According to the tradition, Sanwariya Seth is the same Girdhar Gopal whom Mirabai worshipped. Another legend says that three idols associated with Krishna were hidden during a period of temple destruction and were rediscovered in 1840 after a cowherd named Bholaram Gurjar dreamed of idols buried beneath the ground. Excavation at the site was said to have revealed three similar statues.Sanwariya Seth thus represents a form of devotion in which the sacred and the everyday economy are closely connected — where the devotee does not merely ask the deity for prosperity but symbolically shares that prosperity with him.Ramdevra, Jaisalmer: Ramsa Peer, Deity of Both FaithsIn western Rajasthan, the shrine of Baba Ramdev at Ramdevra represents yet another extraordinary dimension of the state's religious culture.Baba Ramdev is revered by Hindus as Baba Ramdev and by Muslims as Ramsa Peer.The principal shrine stands at the site where Baba Ramdev is believed to have taken samadhi. What began as a small umbrella-shaped structure was expanded into a larger temple by Maharaja Ganga Singh of Bikaner in 1912.An eternal flame burns near the samadhi, while devotees traditionally tie cloth, sacred threads and coconuts while making wishes and later untie them when those wishes are believed to have been fulfilled.The shrine also contains a tomb alongside the idol of Baba Ramdev, reflecting the traditions through which he is revered by both Hindu and Muslim devotees.Several sacred sites around the main temple add to the religious landscape. The samadhi and stone bracelet of Dali Bai, described as a devoted disciple of Ramdevji, are deeply revered. A local belief holds that passing through the bracelet brings healing, and devotees consider the act an important part of their pilgrimage.The stories surrounding Baba Ramdev also emphasise social equality. His opposition to caste discrimination and untouchability and his efforts towards the uplift of women and Dalits are also known. His teachings continue to survive through folk songs known as Harjas.The annual fair at Ramdevra brings this folk devotion into a vast collective expression. Devotees carry white or multicoloured flags, sing praises of Baba Ramdev and offer the flags at the main temple. People of different faiths, including large numbers of tribal devotees, participate in the celebrations.Salasar Balaji, Churu: The Bearded HanumanRajasthan's distinctive temple traditions extend to Salasar Balaji, where the story of the shrine begins with the devotion of Shri Mohandas Ji Maharaj and his intense faith in Lord Hanuman.According to the temple tradition, Hanuman appeared in the form of an idol at Asota village in 1755 and fulfilled Mohandas Ji's devotional wish. The idol was subsequently brought to Salasar, where the temple was constructed in 1759.The story is filled with visions and signs. Mohandas Ji repeatedly experienced divine encounters and eventually received the promise that Lord Hanuman would remain with him in Salasar in idol form. When an idol was discovered while a farmer was working his field at Asota, the local landholder was informed. A voice was then said to have instructed him that the idol should be taken to Salasar.An especially distinctive detail is the form of the idol. According to the temple's tradition, Mohandas Ji had seen Hanuman in a form with a beard and moustache and subsequently incorporated those features into the idol. The lamps lit in 1755 are also said to have remained continuously lit.The temple has another deeply rooted devotional practice: devotees tie coconuts as a form of prayer and wish-making. The tradition says that these coconuts are tied in large numbers as expressions of faith and are not used for other purposes.A Rajasthan where every shrine tells a different storyTaken together, these temples reveal a side of Rajasthan that cannot be captured by architecture alone.Their uniqueness is not merely in what visitors see. It lies in what generations of devotees have believed, remembered and passed down.Rajasthan's temples, in these stories, are not only structures of stone, marble or sandstone. They are repositories of collective memory — places where legends remain alive through ritual, where offerings carry personal meaning, and where faith has found forms as varied as the land itself.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Jaipur | Silver Rate in Jaipur | Bank Holidays in Jaipur | Public Holidays in Jaipur | Jaipur AQI | Weather in Jaipur | Petrol Price in Jaipur | Diesel Price in Jaipur | CNG Price in Jaipur | LPG Price in JaipurStay updated with the latest Jaipur news. articles.title: Conservatives urge Andy Burnham to rule out tax rises at Budget
articles.summary: Shadow chancellor Andrew Griffith says rumours of further taxes are "causing Britain's wealth creators to flee the country".
articles.body:
The Conservatives are urging Prime Minister Andy Burnham and Chancellor John Healey to rule out tax rises at next month's Budget.

In his first major speech as shadow chancellor Andrew Griffith said businesses were "suffering enough" and that rumours of higher taxes were "causing Britain's wealth creators to flee the country".

He also promised to replace tax rules for self-employed workers, who he said had been "badly let down" by the system.

Labour said: "Andrew Griffith has made the Conservatives' priorities clear: scrapping hard-won workers' rights, while promising tax cuts with no explanation of how they would pay for them or which public services would be cut."

The Labour spokesperson added: "The Tories should be apologising for crashing the economy thanks to Griffith's old boss Liz Truss – not asking working people to pay the price all over again."

The chancellor is due to set out his Budget on 28 October against a backdrop of rising inflation and global energy prices.

On Thursday, trade unions will meet the chancellor to push for their proposals, with the Unite union urging the government to reverse the freezing of tax thresholds.

Burnham has warned that the Budget would be "challenging" due to the war in the Middle East but insisted he was prepared to take "difficult decisions" on the economy.

Call to raise tax thresholds among union demands ahead of Budget

Burnham rejects 'tax and spend socialist' comments

Faisal Islam: Chancellor's attempts to boost vibes may limit tax rises

Griffith - who was appointed as shadow chancellor last month - told an audience at a further education college that taxes in the UK had reached "nosebleed territory" and that Healey "must end uncertainty today and rule out any new taxes".

"He must rule out increasing taxes on small businesses and the self-employed."

Griffith described business owners and the self-employed as "economic heroes", adding: "Any government worth its salt would do everything it could to help them because whilst not every acorn grows into a mighty oak we need green shoots that are nurtured not trampled upon."

He said the IR35 regime had "crushed the dreams of self-employed people" and promised that a Conservative government would "replace it with a new system that respects the right of the self-employed to choose their status and only prevents actual abuse".

The IR35 rules are designed to prevent people avoiding tax by posing as self-employed contractors rather than employees but some freelancers argue the system has led to unfair treatment.

Griffith also urged the chancellor to pause the rollout of Making Tax Digital, the new system for the self-employed to register their income with HMRC.

"For the self-employed, many of whom will have started out in colleges such as this, there is this special torture of Making Tax Digital."

He acknowledged that the previous Conservative government had been responsible for setting up the system and said that "despite well-intentioned, the execution has left a lot to be desired".

Griffith told the audience that he had commissioned Lord Mackinlay of Richborough, the former South Thanet MP , and Robert Colvile, the outgoing director of the Centre for Policy Studies think tank, to produce a report on reducing regulations for small businesses.

Over the weekend, the Mail on Sunday reported that the Conservatives could promise to abolish inheritance tax if they win the next election, with the policy potentially being announced at the party's annual conference in October.

Speaking to the BBC ahead of his speech, Griffith said he would "love" to cut the tax but it would have to be "subject to an ability to set out properly how we would fund that".

"I'm going to be responsible and only want to make promises I can keep," he said.

He added that he had recently been on a fact-finding trip to Sweden, which scrapped inheritance taxes in 2005.

Reform UK has previously said it wanted to cut inheritance tax, but speaking at the party's conference, the party's Treasury spokesman Robert Jenrick said it would not be a priority.

"It's a bold chancellor that would say I'd rather privilege 36,000 families than 40 million [income] taxpayers," he told a Reform conference fringe event.

Asked if getting rid of inheritance tax would amount to a tax cut for the wealthy, Griffith argued that it would boost growth and that the wealthiest people were often able to "arrange their affairs" to avoid the tax.
